items.title: DoGBench: The first user-facing docs generation benchmark. No model scores >50%
items.summary: Article URL: https://dogbench.ai/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49928118 Points: 4 # Comments: 1
items.content:
Can agents meet expert standards for user-facing documentation?

DoGBench evaluates agents that write and maintain user-facing software documentation in response to real repository events and reported documentation gaps. Each patch is scored with rubrics validated with project maintainers. The scores measure progress toward that standard, not performance relative to a human expert.

Promptless: This was the same production agent available to all Promptless customers. We made no specific agent improvements based on the DogBench work.

Cloud agent caveat: Cloud-based agents were instructed not to use the internet. We verified that Promptless did not browse the internet to find contaminating information, but we could not verify this for other cloud agents.

Submit your agent’s DoGBench results for review. We review submissions manually and will follow up about verification and evaluation requirements.

For documentation owners who want to use this research in a discussion with their teams or leadership about the challenges of technical writing and where today’s AI agents fall short, we’ve prepared a concise slide deck.

AI agents can write polished documentation, but they often miss what readers need to complete a task. DoGBench evaluates whether agents can recognize when documentation needs updating and produce changes that meet expert review standards.

The benchmark contains 292 tasks drawn from real open-source projects, including Helm, PostHog, Mautic, and Doc Detective. Of these, 205 require a documentation change; 87 require leaving the documentation unchanged. Tasks include creating new documentation, updating existing guidance, and deleting stale or redundant content. Our primary evaluation uses a random, stratified 117-item held-out split: 82 requiring updates and 35 requiring no change. For reproducibility, we are publishing 735 complete agent trajectories from seven non-cloud agents.

Documentation work begins with a judgment: does this change affect users, and do they need new guidance?

Agents make mistakes in both directions. Some document internal refactors or performance optimizations that require no new user guidance. Others overlook necessary updates because they find no existing page about the feature, even when that missing coverage is the problem they need to solve.

Among the seven model-and-harness lanes reported in the paper, the highest combined score on the 117-item held-out split was 47.3 out of 100 , achieved by Qwen3.8 Max with OpenCode. The leaderboard also includes three cloud-agent systems evaluated on that same split.

A patch can sound clear and contain correct facts while omitting a prerequisite, decision point, or essential step. It can also appear on a page readers are unlikely to find or contradict guidance elsewhere.

These categories overlap. Fabricated content, such as invented classes, flags, or endpoints, appeared in 6.1% of submissions. With frontier agents, hallucinations can also take subtler forms: distorting real functionality by extending its scope, misstating defaults, or presenting behavior that holds only under specific conditions as universally true. Our audit classified these distortions as technical inaccuracies.

The trajectory analysis also found that agents frequently missed decisive evidence or stopped investigating after finding the first plausible page to edit.

A patch is P0-clean when it has no critical failures under the rubric.

Documentation owners bring context that a code change alone may not reveal: who the reader is, what they are trying to accomplish, and how the change affects their workflow. That context helps determine whether an update is needed and what it must cover.

Review an agent’s draft against that workflow. Check that the reader can find the guidance, complete the steps, and verify the result. Confirm the conditions behind each technical claim and check related pages for contradictions or stale instructions.

Each agent received a repository as it existed before the change and a triggering signal, such as a code pull request or a reported documentation gap. The merged documentation was withheld.

We evaluated seven agent lanes on the same task set. Task-specific rubrics assessed accuracy, completeness, reader guidance, placement, style, and repository conventions. Across the 205 documentation-needed items, the current rubrics contain 3,273 criteria, including 798 P0 criteria.

DoGBench reports update decisions and patch quality separately. The scoring rules capture both:

items.title: Apple's smart home camera reportedly won't record video
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.theapplepost.com/2026/10/01/72882/apples-smart-home-camera-reportedly-wont-record-video/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49928054 Points: 8 # Comments: 1
items.content:
Apple’s upcoming smart home camera is reportedly taking a very different approach to products from Ring and Google Nest, with the device designed to understand what is happening around the home without recording video for users to watch back.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, speaking on the new Power On podcast, says Apple’s camera will have “no video recording.” Instead, the device will use AI to analyze its surroundings and report what it detects.

The unusual approach could make privacy one of the defining features of Apple’s first dedicated home camera, while also making the product fundamentally different from a conventional security camera.

The device, known internally as J450, is expected to use a low-frame-rate camera alongside facial recognition and infrared sensors to identify people and pets around the home.

Rather than presenting a continuous or recorded video feed, it could provide information about activity in the house and use what it sees to power automations.

That could allow Apple’s Home system to recognize when someone enters or leaves a room, switch lights off when a room becomes empty, or adjust music and other settings depending on which household member is present.

Bloomberg has reported that Apple is planning a much broader push into smart home hardware , beginning with its new HomePad hub, HomePod mini 2, and Apple TV 4K.

The Apple Post previously reported on the J450 camera as part of Apple’s wider smart home roadmap , including its expected use of facial recognition and infrared sensing.

Gurman’s latest comments clarify an important part of how the camera could work: despite having a camera sensor, the product isn’t being designed around giving customers a library of recorded footage.

That would separate it from Apple’s existing HomeKit Secure Video system, which lets compatible third-party cameras securely stream and store encrypted recordings in iCloud.

It could also create limitations for customers who expect a security camera to provide footage after a break-in, package theft, or other incident. How Apple’s wider security system would handle those situations remains unclear.

Apple is reportedly developing a home security and monitoring service alongside the hardware, suggesting the J450 may be intended as one component of a larger system rather than a direct replacement for every traditional security camera.

The camera is expected to follow Apple’s initial HomePad launch rather than arrive alongside it this month, with previous Bloomberg reporting pointing to 2027 for Apple’s broader home security push.

items.title: What happened in the failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?
items.summary: The convicted killer is in hospital in Tennessee after surviving two lethal injections, in a case that has raised many questions.
items.content:
US convicted murderer Christa Pike is in a critical condition in hospital after Tennessee authorities failed to execute her by lethal injection, her lawyer says.

The case of Pike, whose attempted execution on Wednesday had already been the subject of a high-profile legal battle, raised a number of questions, including what went wrong? And what happens next?

A third-party review has been ordered by state Governor Bill Lee, who has halted executions in Tennessee for the rest of the year.

Pike, now 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder a year earlier of 19-year-old Colleen Slemmer.

Pike was scheduled to be put to death in Tennessee on Wednesday evening local time. The injections were allowed by the Supreme Court at the 11th hour.

Pike was given two injections of the drug pentobarbital, but her legal team said these failed to stop her heartbeat and that she could still be heard snoring.

Tennessee halts executions after death row inmate Christa Pike survives hers

US death row inmate survives execution attempt after two lethal injections

The Tennessee Department of Correction has defended the method it used, saying "the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out".

The state protocol does not clearly specify what should happen if an inmate remains alive after a second dose, according to the AP news agency.

Authorities are yet to say whether they will try again to execute Pike. They have not explained why the dosage given to Pike was non-fatal.

Opponents of the death penalty said it was difficult to know what went wrong, because part of Pike's execution happened behind a curtain.

Maya Foa, the head of international legal organisation Reprieve, said: "Lethal injection relies on secrecy at every stage, to hide the violence of the state taking a human life."

The Tennessee correction department said Pike had been taken to an off-site medical facility, while one of her lawyers said on Wednesday that she was being given "life-saving measures" in hospital.

On Thursday, lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters: "We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment."

Dr Joel Zivot, a professor at the Emory University School of Medicine, told the BBC in an email: "It's very possible that as a consequence of the delay of the beginning of resuscitation she [Pike] will have a brain injury."

Historically, the US Supreme Court has not halted second attempts at executions, said John Mills, a lawyer who works with inmates sentenced to death.

In 2024, it allowed Alabama to proceed with a second execution of Kenneth Eugene Smith, using an experimental oxygen deprivation method, after their attempt to kill him by lethal injection failed two years earlier.

A notable Supreme Court case from 1947 allowed the state of Louisiana to try a second electrocution of Willie Smith, a teenager whose first execution attempt failed when he was 17 years old.

The court found a second execution would not violate the Constitution's prohibitions against double jeopardy or cruel and unusual punishment and Smith was executed aged 18.

"If the question is, is it likely the federal courts would intervene in a second attempt? I'm afraid the answer is a resounding no," Mills said of Pike's case.

Pentobarbital is a potent sedative that slows down the body, including the nervous system. Doctors sometimes use it as a treatment for certain conditions, but in high doses it can also be used as a lethal injection to cause death.

Its use in lethal injections came under renewed scrutiny last year after a US federal government review during the Biden administration raised concerns about the drug's potential for "unnecessary pain and suffering".

The Biden government banned its use in federal executions, but that did not bind individual states such as Tennessee, which can choose their own methods.

In recent years, states have found some drugs needed for lethal injections harder to come by, because pharmaceutical companies have opposed the use of their products for such purposes.

The Tennessee correction department has not specifically addressed an allegation from Pike's legal team that the pentobarbital it used was "degraded".

But the department said in a statement the lethal injection chemical had "consistently been effective".

The attempted execution of Pike was not the first in Tennessee in 2026 that did not go to plan.

The execution of Tony Carruthers, who was convicted of kidnapping and murdering three people in 1994, was postponed in May after staff were unable to find a vein for a lethal injection. He was granted a year's reprieve by the governor.

In 2022, more than a third of executions across the US were botched or highly problematic, according to the Death Penalty Information Center.

Colleen Slemmer's killers met at a job training camp for troubled teens.

She was found with an inverted pentagram - a symbol associated with satanic groups - carved into her chest.

Pike had accused Colleen of insulting her and trying to steal her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, who was 17.

Two other residents at the camp later testified that Pike had bragged about the murder and showed them a piece of Colleen's skull.

Colleen's mum, May Martinez, drove 11 hours from Florida to attend the execution, she told People , external , alongside with her husband Raul.

She said: "I wanted her [Pike] to remember who Colleen was and what they've done and never forget that thought, no matter where she goes."

Shipp was given a life sentence with the possibility of parole and he remains in prison.

He was spared the death penalty for his part in the attack because he was not yet legally an adult at the time.

items.title: Christa Pike in critical condition after surviving two lethal injections, lawyer says
items.summary: Pike’s lawyers have asked for her death sentence to be commuted following the botched execution.
items.content:
Tennessee death row inmate Christa Pike is in "critical condition, receiving life-saving care" at hospital, after surviving two lethal injection attempts, leading the state's governor to halt all executions for the year.

"We don't have a sense of her prognosis or much update on her health at the moment," her lawyer Randy Spivey told reporters on Thursday. "But we do know that she is alive right now."

Her lawyers are now asking for her sentence to be commuted. Pike, 50, was sentenced to death in 1996 for the murder of Colleen Slemmer.

She was injected with two lethal doses of pentobarbital on Wednesday but remained alive, her lawyers said. She was then sent to hospital in an ambulance.

Pike was 18 when she and her then-boyfriend, Tadaryl Shipp, beat, tortured and killed 19-year-old Slemmer.

Her attempted execution on Wednesday was the subject of a last-minute legal battle. This culminated in the US Supreme Court allowing the lethal injections to go ahead.

Slemmer's mother May Martinez, who was among those who wanted the execution to take place and who travelled to Tennessee to witness it, told NBC News after the botched attempt that "it was a mess".

On Thursday afternoon, Pike's lawyers offered more details about what happened during the attempted execution, describing a harrowing scene shrouded in secrecy.

"Last night, the execution team attempted to establish an IV line for an hour," Spivey said. "I counted at least seven needles used in her left arm alone, one of which appeared to be bent when it was pulled from her arm after an unsuccessful attempt."

Spivey said that observers were kept in a dark room behind a closed curtain, after the second lethal dose had been administered and "it was clear that Miss Pike was still breathing" minutes later.

"No-one knew what was going on behind that curtain," Spivey said. "I had no idea when and if medical professionals began to assist."

Spivey said the state's governor must commute Christa's sentence now, a request that was denied previously.

Stephen Ferrell, another of Pike's lawyers, said they were also looking at other legal options.

"We want to think this through and we want to make sure that Christa recovers and has some input in what she wants," he said.

Tennessee Governor Bill Lee has ordered an independent review and said on Thursday the investigation into Pike's botched execution "will be thorough", adding that "it's going to take time".

"There are a lot of questions," Lee said. "The people of our state deserve to have those questions answered, and that's what this investigation is for."

Lee has not made clear who will conduct the independent review of the state's execution procedures.

His order to pause all executions will overlap with the planned 3 December execution of convicted murderer Gary Sutton.

The Tennessee Department of Correction, which handled the execution, issued a statement defending its handling of the case.

It said in a statement that it "followed every step of the State's lawful, established execution protocol approved by the attorney general's office".

"The lethal injection chemical in the protocol has consistently been effective, and the protocol does not allow for additional procedures beyond what was carried out this evening."

Pike was given two doses of the chemical pentobarbital, in accordance with state protocol when the first attempt fails, but was still alive afterwards, according to court filings by her lawyers.

"This execution is causing Ms Pike unnecessary agony and occurring in violation of his right to be executed free of cruel and unusual punishment," her lawyers said.

The Tennessee attorney general's office said in a statement that it agreed with the decision to call for an investigation, adding: "We need to know what happened."

US Republican Senator Marsha Blackburn, who is running for Tennessee governor, described the situation as "tragic".

"While there should be a thorough review of what happened and why the process failed, the answer is simple: bring back the electric chair," Blackburn said.

Democrat Jerri Green, Blackburn's opponent, criticised her for wanting to "bring back one of the most cruel forms of capital punishment".

"As governor, I would put a moratorium on all future executions," Green said on X.

This is the second time in 2026 Tennessee officials attempted and failed to execute a prisoner.

In May, the execution of Tony Carruthers was called off after staff were unable to find a vein to administer a lethal drug. Carruthers was given a year's reprieve.

With additional reporting by Stephanie Hegarty, World Service correspondent

US death row inmate survives execution attempt after two lethal injections

What happened in failed execution of Christa Pike - and what next?

items.title: Aweb – Communication for AI Agents
items.summary: Article URL: https://aweb.ai Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49927587 Points: 12 # Comments: 5
items.content:
aweb gives agents stable identities, durable mail and chat, and wake-up events across sessions, runtimes, and machines. Independently operated servers can federate with one another.

The CLI and API are runtime-independent. Maintained wake-up integrations are available for Claude Code and Pi; other runtimes can consume the event stream.

llms.txt contains the same product and setup information in plain text.

Alice runs in Claude Code. Bob runs in Pi on another machine. Alice sends a message; aweb stores it, wakes Bob through the Pi extension, and delivers Bob's reply to Alice. If Bob is offline, the message waits until he returns.

The message is durable server state. A wake-up event tells the runtime that work is waiting; the agent then fetches the message by ID.

When the sender needs an immediate answer, chat waits for the recipient:

Install once. Then start Claude Code with the channel loaded and permission prompts off:

Incoming mail and chat are then presented inside the session. Channel messages reach the session only in bypass-permissions mode today; in the default auto mode they arrive and are not shown. Claude Code asks once to confirm the development-channels flag. Full setup →

Install once; Pi wakes when mail, chat, or tasks arrive. aweb for Pi →

aweb provides identity, authentication, durable delivery, wake-up, message history, access control, and federation.

Install the CLI and run aw init to give an agent an identity and connect it. Start with two agents; add machines, teams, and organizations without replacing the communication layer. The same addresses and protocol continue to work as the system grows.

Because addressing and federation are open, an agent can communicate beyond the server or organization where it began.

Any agent that can call the CLI, HTTP API, MCP tools, or event stream can use aweb .

aweb stores and delivers messages, maintains identity and addressing, and emits delivery and wake-up events.

Messages are server state, not session scrollback. A message remains available after either agent's session ends and while the recipient is offline. Fetch any message later by ID.

A delivery event signals that work is waiting. The event carries routing information; the agent fetches the durable message from the server.

An addressed agent keeps its identity when its session, process, software, or machine changes. Private signing keys stay with the agent or its chosen custodian.

An agent can accept first contact from any verified sender or restrict delivery to verified team members and explicit contacts. Team membership is carried by signed certificates.

Organizations can operate separate servers and exchange signed messages. They do not need a shared account, runtime, or model provider.

The aweb server, AWID registry, and aw CLI are MIT licensed. The hosted service runs the same communication server that can be run independently.

An AWID address has the form domain/name . Trust begins in DNS: the namespace controller authorizes the team controller, the team controller signs membership certificates, and each agent signs with its own key. Recipients can verify that chain without trusting the communication server to define identity.

With an aweb.ai namespace, aweb operates the namespace and team authority. With Bring Your Own Team (BYOT), your organization uses its own domain and retains the namespace and team controller keys. The hosted aweb service can deliver messages for that team, but it cannot add members or manufacture team authority.

Server hosting, team authority, and agent-key custody are separate choices.

Stores mail and chat, emits delivery and wake-up events, tracks presence, and provides a shared task queue. Conversations remain available independently of any agent session.

Publishes and resolves the namespace, address, team, membership, and key-history facts in the AWID trust chain. It verifies signed authority; it does not hold a self-custodial agent's private key.

The command-line client used by agents and humans: initialize, send, reply, read mail, wait in chat, consume events, and inspect configuration.

Presents incoming mail, chat, and control events inside a Claude Code session.

Wakes Pi when mail, chat, or tasks arrive and installs the aweb skills used with the CLI.

Other agents can consume the same event stream. Hosted, the services run at app.aweb.ai and api.awid.ai. Self-hosted, both services run from the aweb repository. Architecture →

The server, AWID registry, and CLI are open source. A local installation starts with Docker Compose:

The hosted service creates the namespace, team, and credentials. No local server is required.

items.title: The death of web development education
items.summary: Article URL: https://molily.de/web-dev-education/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49927100 Points: 137 # Comments: 107
items.content:
In a personal blog post, Baldur Bjarnason describes how he worked in various fields and positions: as an author, publisher, consultant, developer, educator, as well as radio and TV producer. None of these jobs were economically viable in the long term.

Adding insult to injury, the respective communities alienate interdisciplinary people who do not fit into their narrow conception of the field. For example, either you are considered as too “technical” for a “creative” job or too “creative” for “technical” job.

Bjarnason describes the impact of generative AI on web development education:

[All] my training and education projects had dropped off one by one. Most of my peers who had been selling courses and training were shutting down their businesses. The demand for web dev ebooks had cratered. […]

Software developers haven’t all switched to using agents for their coding, but they do seem to have all switched to error-prone, backwards-facing, nondeterministic chatbots for what now passes as web dev “education”.

Many independent educators who used to earn a living from web development training and developer relations have reported that GenAI has ruined their business.

Axel Rauschmayer is one of the world’s most prolific writers on JavaScript and TypeScript. He used to publish his e-books as free online books . Since 2005, he has explained the details of ECMAScript and other web technologies in his influential blog 2ality . Now he writes:

The income from my book sales went from being enough for me to live off (2024) to zero (2026).

The traffic to my blog and my books (which were free to read online) increased beyond what I can currently afford. Virtually all of it comes from AI crawlers, so there is no ad income.

Therefore, I’m taking my blog and my books offline so that I can decide what to do next – especially w.r.t. AI companies stealing my work.

( Rauschmayer still sells his books on JavaScript and TypeScript for a reasonable price! )

Salma Alam-Naylor used to work in Developer Relations , a role under constant pressure to justify its existence. Companies expect DevRel to generate short-term financial gain – which it cannot by nature. This lead Alam-Naylor to burnout and anxiety. In this situation, she writes that AI is killing developer education :

[Developers] aren’t gathering together in online spaces to learn and teach and share exciting projects anymore, rather they are mindlessly scrolling for a much-needed hit of short-form content dopamine (because the horrors of the world are more persistent than ever). […] [Many] developers have replaced authentic human collaboration with conversations with the dreaded Chat Bots. […]

The future feels bleak for educators. Rich curriculums we craft intentionally and carefully for real human audiences are now routinely stolen and regurgitated by predictive algorithms. The Chat Bots, with their sycophantic tone of voice, are deliberately engineered to erase our own personalities, hard work and craft entirely from the equation.

The only conclusion I can draw from this is that my experience, skills, empathy and teaching expertise no longer hold the value they once did in this volatile industry (if they ever really did?).

Alam-Naylor decided to accept a lower-paid developer job without public exposure. She decided to go offline.

She cites Josh W. Comeau , who creates online courses, well-researched articles and interactive tutorials on web technologies. GenAI has destroyed his business model as well :

I’ve spoken to a few course creators now, and we’re all seeing the same trend. Revenue down 50%+. Fewer people engaging with our content. People switching to LLMs, which slurp up all of our work and regurgitate it, without consent or compensation.

Comeau notes that with LLMs, there’s no incentive for people to make high-quality free content.

YouTube content creator Kyle Cook from Web Dev Simplified reported that the views on his programming tutorials and thereby his income essentially dropped by half .

I’m making half the money I was making exactly one year ago. [This] is definitely not sustainable for a full-time job. […] [There’s] almost no incentive as a creator of content to create programming content when it makes practically no money and is incredibly difficult to make when I could just make a video about the latest AI model, which is easy to make, makes more money, and gets more views. […] There’s almost no reason to make programming content anymore. The only reason I do it is because I find value in it. I find enjoyment in it. And I’m able to make money through other means rather than just YouTube ad revenue.

Rachel Andrew is a renowned technical writer and editor of many books and articles on web topics. In a series of blog posts , she reflects on the impact of GenAI on technical publishing. She reports that GenAI has broken the relationship between subject matter experts – the authors of the original draft – and editors who proof-read, fact-check and polish the article.

Editors have to apply extra scrutiny because AI tools might have introduced subtle inaccuracies without the original authors being aware of it. AI can be very confidently wrong, and if the text seems clear, it’s possible to miss that it’s clearly nonsense. Authors want to save some time, but create additional work for the editing team.

Andrew sees LLMs as a useful tool but emphasizes that its field of application is very limited and its output needs to be reviewed by people who deeply care about the end result .

She further questions whether AI actually increases productivity . Potential productivity gains stem from GenAI automating certain tasks. These tasks can as well be automated without AI, Andrew says, AI just makes it more accessible to non-coders. Now that more information, like API references, is made available in a machine-readable format for LLMs, it’s easier to perform non-AI automations.

Again Andrew argues that perceived individual productivity benefits might come from shifting the work onto someone else . For example, writers shift the work onto technical editors or even the readers. [You] might feel more productive, but all you’ve done is move the work around, make someone else’s job or experience measurably worse, and reduce quality. In summary, she asks (emphasis mine):

How can we justify the cost (financial, environmental, and human) of AI, if the reality is a relatively small bump in productivity that could have happened by teaching more people to automate tasks using existing tools or simple coding? Why aren’t businesses encouraging people to use non-AI methods where possible, saving the AI only for where it adds value? Given the societal costs, and the benefit to a business of bringing onboard and training people , perhaps on a balance of things even those tasks where AI is needed are better performed by people.

First and foremost, I would like to acknowledge these experiences and amplify these voices. GenAI has catastrophic effects on web development education and learning. It threatens the livelihoods of writers, teachers and communicators who make web technologies approachable and accessible, who nurture the next generation of web authors and developers.

There is no obvious short-term solution. This does not stop some people from posting knee-jerk reactions. I won’t link to these blog posts, but they go like this:

These reactions are in essence the same as “you gotta jump on the AI train or you’ll perish”. Such comments are merely turning the knife in the wound.

I cannot give those educators any advice. But I do imagine a more compassionate reaction:

I highly appreciate your work as an educator, writer, researcher, or free and open-source software developer. A heartfelt thank you. I am sorry that AI sucks all joy out of you and your profession.

I acknowledge that AI companies appropriate your labor, destroy your economic livelihood and threaten the foundations of your field.

This very situation won’t get better with more AI, better AI, or developing with or for AI.

In a situation where Big Tech teamed up with fascist movements, it sounds far-fetched, but the bare minimum would be to force the AI oligarchs to pay for the crisis they are imposing on the web community, among others. We need to expropriate the expropriators.

Against the destruction of web development education, I’d like to hold up certain values. In a previous blog post , I described how I once entered web development through a volunteer-driven, non-commercial documentation project.

Such initiatives democratized the web as they helped a wide range of people to establish their own web sites and communities – local businesses, self-employed professionals, art and craft groups, neighborhood initiatives, schools and kindergartens, sports clubs, LGBTQ+ folks, fandoms etc.

Today, we often hear the word “democratize” from GenAI promoters, but it means the exact opposite. AI centralizes power and commodifies knowledge, instead of teaching skills and deep understanding.

The web is a radical democratic medium. Right now, tech oligarchs and fascist movements are trying to dismantle its radical potential . We must ensure that everyone can shape the web.

items.title: Poker Portogallo, prima gioia per Klopp. Dublino, in campo palline con la bandiera della Palestina
items.summary: Goncalo Ramos non fa rimpiangere Ronaldo, i lusitani vincono 4-2 in Danimarca. La Germania batte 2-0 la Serbia. Altro gesto di protesta contro Israele durante Irlanda-Austria
items.content:
Abbandonato da Cristiano Ronaldo e con Leao promosso titolare con la maglia n. 7, il Portogallo vince (2-4) anche a Copenhagen con la Danimarca , resta in testa a punteggio pieno (9 punti) nel gruppo 4 di Lega A e ipoteca un posto nei quarti di finale di Nations League . La squadra di Jorge Jesus ha centrato un palo con Gonçalo Ramos e poi ha sbloccato il risultato (13’) con Joao Cancelo , imbeccato in area proprio dal centravanti del Milan. Leao ha sciupato per due volte il raddoppio e ha consentito alla Danimarca di pareggiare (23’) con un bel destro a giro di Damsgaard .

Il Portogallo si è rimboccato le maniche e già al 26’ è tornato avanti con un sinistro sul primo palo di Gonçalo Ramos , lanciato a rete da Bruno Fernandes. La Danimarca ha reagito con orgoglio e al 53’ ha di nuovo pareggiato con Hojlund che, lanciato a rete da Damsgaard, ha superato Diogo Costa in uscita con uno 'scavino' di sinistro e poi ha omaggiato Ronaldo esultando alla sua maniera. Il Portogallo non si è disunito e al 67’ si è riportato in vantaggio con un colpo di testa di Vitinha su cross di Bruno Fernandes. A chiudere i conti poi, nel finale, ha pensato il subentrato Joao Felix (3° gol in 3 partite) girando in rete un assist di Dalot.

Nell’altra gara del girone il Galles piega in rimonta (2-1) la Norvegia e torna in corsa per il secondo posto. Gli scandinavi si sono illusi dopo la rete all’11’ di Bobb . Sono stati raggiunti al 38’ da James e si sono complicati la vita in avvio di ripresa quando sono rimasti in 10 per l’espulsione del ‘bolognese’ Heggem, reo di un fallo ai danni di James lanciato a rete. Il Galles ne ha subito approfittato trasformando (48’) la susseguente punizione dal limite con Neco Williams .

Nel gruppo A Jurgen Klopp si toglie la soddisfazione di cogliere il primo successo con la Germania superando per 2-0 a Monaco la Serbia . Ha sbloccato il risultato al 40’ Bischof , alla seconda presenza in nazionale, riprendendo un tiro di Wirtz respinto dal palo. Ha raddoppiato al 61’ lo stesso Wirtz servito in area da Mittelstadt. La Germania resta al 3°posto perché l’ Olanda ha strappato un prezioso punto a Salonicco rimontando la Grecia da 2-0 a 2-2. Ellenici illusi dai gol nel primo tempo di Ioannidis e Masouras ma ripresi da Van Dijk e, nel finale, dall'ex milanista Reijnders .

Tra le altre gare da segnalare, in Lega B, la rimonta (da 2-0 a 2-2) dell' Austria a Dublino contro l' Irlanda . Un risultato che consente a Schmid e compagni di conservare il primato solitario nel gruppo 3. I padroni di casa si erano illusi dopo la doppietta nel primo tempo di Parrott , autore di un gol strepitoso, 'alla Roberto Baggio', dopo aver saltato in dribbling tutta la difesa avversaria. Prass e Gregoritsch hanno rimesso le cose a posto nella ripresa. La gara era stata interrotta per 2' al 13' per togliere dal campo alcune palline da tennis rivestite con i colori della Palestina che erano state lanciate in campo in segno di protesta contro il genocidio di Israele nella Striscia di Gaza.

items.title: Renee Good: Family of US woman killed by ICE agent sues Trump officials
items.summary: Lawyers for Good's family say US officials created "an unprecedented environment for state sponsored violence" in Minneapolis.
items.content:
The family of a woman who was killed by an immigration agent in Minneapolis has announced two lawsuits against the US government and members of the Trump administration.

Renee Good, a US citizen, was shot to death by an Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) officer during a major immigration sweep in January. Millions watched the video recorded of her killing and residents of the Minnesota city took to the streets to protest.

One lawsuit blames the government for her death, claiming the operation created "an unprecedented environment for state-sponsored violence", a lawyer for the family said.

A White House spokeswoman in a statement called the lawsuits "baseless".

The lawsuits were brought by Good's brother, Brent Ganger, and her partner, Becca Good.

Speaking publicly for the first time since the shooting, Becca Good told a news conference on the lawsuits on Thursday: "The whole world had to watch as our entire universe was destroyed."

"We were all robbed," she said as she described how the shooting affected their three children.

In one of the lawsuits, the family accuses the government of "battery, assault, false imprisonment, intentional infliction of emotional distress and negligence that caused Renee's death", according to the family's lawyer.

It cites the Federal Tort Claims Act, which allows citizens to sue the government for personal injury, death or property damage caused by the negligence of federal employees.

The second lawsuit targets ICE officer Jonathan Ross, who shot Good, as well as White House Deputy Chief of Staff Stephen Miller, former Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem, White House border tsar Tom Homan and others, alleging a "conspiracy to interfere with civil rights by senior federal officials, federal immigration enforcement agents and private actors".

"Our government has become a grave and mortal threat to its own citizens," the family's lawyer, Antonio Romanucci told Thursday's news conference.

In her statement, Lauren Bis, a spokeswoman for the White House, said the deaths of Americans at the hands of illegal immigrants should merit "equal coverage" by news media.

She also said the government will "vigorously defend these baseless civil lawsuits".

Trump had initially blamed Good's own actions for her death, saying just hours after she was killed that she "violently, wilfully and viciously ran over the ICE officer". Weeks later, he called her death a "tragedy" and said agents were sometimes "going to make a mistake".

The White House also shared a comment from Trump where he said: "I would bet you that she, under normal circumstances, was a very solid, wonderful person - but her actions were pretty tough."

He also said ICE agents' work "is being made very difficult" and that "when you look at the way that car was pulled away… there are a couple versions of that tape that are very very bad," according to the comments.

Good was a 37-year-old mother of three who had just moved to the city. She was shot on 7 January in a traffic stop, which immigration authorities said occurred after she made "an attempt to kill or cause bodily harm to agents". Witnesses disputed that she had been attempting to attack officers.

Her death sparked nationwide protests that intensified after another Minneapolis resident, Alex Pretti, was killed by immigration agents on 24 January.

Weeks later, hundreds of federal agents were withdrawn from the city and the official in charge of the operation, Greg Bovino, was removed from his post.

Granger, Good's brother, said at Thursday's news conference that "since her death no meaningful change has occurred".

"Our family is waiting and we will wait no longer," he said.

At least 10 people have been killed in encounters with immigration officers during Trump's second term, which began in January 2025, according to the Associated Press.

On Tuesday, Good's mother testified at a congressional hearing, saying: "I am a registered Republican. I voted for President Trump under the impression that these agents were here to protect the citizens of the United States.

"But far more than being a Republican, I am a Christian," she continued. "Jesus teaches us to forgive and I have, but what we are asking for is accountability."

The ICE raids are over, but some Minnesotans say they still live in fear

Newly released video undermines ICE account of Minneapolis migrant shooting

items.title: Automatic Transmission – a data-privacy study of connected vehicles
items.summary: Article URL: https://automatictransmission.khoury.northeastern.edu/index.html Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49926628 Points: 132 # Comments: 128
items.content:
This diagram shows the data flows to and from a vehicle and its companion mobile app. Both devices send data, including private consumer data, to different 1st and 3rd party servers using Wi-Fi and cellular service. Solid arrows represent flows that were intercepted through our experiments.

Once the data gets sent to these servers, it is up to the companies that receive the consumer information to make decisions on what they do with it. Unfortunately, in many cases, this includes sharing or selling consumer data to other undisclosed 3rd parties. Consumers have no control over their data once it has left their device

In this paper, we take the first steps to address the limited visibility into the privacy implications of the connected vehicle ecosystem. We identify two vantage points in the ecosystem where we can gain insight into the data that connected vehicles are sharing with both manufacturers and third parties: the vehicles themselves and the mobile apps provided by manufacturers. We ask the following guiding questions:

We investigated 21 vehicles from the U.S. market in a controlled environment along with 30 companion mobile apps instrumented with on-site vehicles between October 2024 and August 2025. Below is a description of the experiments we ran and our setup.

To collect Wi-Fi traffic from vehicles, we configured a custom access point (AP) on a Raspberry Pi and used tcpdump to log all packets that were sent or received via this AP. This allowed us to see all the destinations the vehicles were sending data to but not the information within the packets as it was encrypted.

One hypothesis we tested was whether blocking a vehicle’s ability to communicate over its cellular network would force more Wi-Fi communication. To block external cellular signals, we drove 11 EVs in the sample into a car-sized Faraday tent providing ≈93 dB of attenuation, blocking their cellular connection entirely. Stationary Idle and Active tests were repeated inside the tent to see whether traffic that normally goes out over cellular rerouted to Wi-Fi instead.

In total, we experimented with 30 connected vehicle companion apps that were paired with the vehicles at Consumer Reports’s testing facility.

* While we tested a wide range of vehicles, we did not cover every manufacturer in the U.S. market. As with all empirical studies, our results should be interpreted as a snapshot in time, and may not generalize to vehicles outside our sample or outside the U.S.

items.title: SvelteKit 3
items.summary: Article URL: https://svelte.dev/blog/sveltekit-3-is-here Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49926536 Points: 88 # Comments: 24
items.content:
Version 3.0 of SvelteKit, the official application framework for Svelte, is now available.

If you’ve used earlier versions of SvelteKit, everything will feel very familiar — it’s the same framework with a little more polish, a little more type safety, and a little less junk. We’ve made migration as seamless as we can with the sv migrate command...

...which will automatically migrate as much of your codebase as possible, and generate a TODO list for everything else. (If you’re agentically inclined, your robot friends will make short work of it.)

As with any major version bump there are a handful of breaking changes to be aware of, which are covered in the migration guide (or, more briefly, in the recent release candidate announcement ).

Remote functions are a set of utilities for secure, efficient, type-safe client-server communication. You’ve likely seen some version of this idea in other frameworks, but we think you’re going to prefer this one.

Using them requires Async Svelte , which for now requires an experimental flag. Bear with us.

This is as good a place as any to remind everyone that the next in-person Svelte Summit is taking place on November 19-20 in the lovely town of Ljubljana, Slovenia. Among other things it will be a celebration of Svelte’s 10th birthday, and we’d love to share some cake with you.

items.title: ArXiv's Updated Rate Limit Policy
items.summary: Article URL: https://blog.arxiv.org/2026/10/01/updated-rate-limit-policy/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=49926512 Points: 60 # Comments: 17
items.content:
arXiv, and the scientific community at large, are facing a watershed moment. Scholarly publishing is currently changing at a rapid pace, and we are seeing a massive transformation in how researchers communicate their results.

Before the advent of AI, there was an easily discernible, practical limit to the rate at which independent submissions could be produced, and arXiv’s volunteer moderators would limit submitters who were well above that threshold. With AI tools becoming more advanced and accessible to authors, the “practical limit” of how many papers can be submitted is now up for debate. As of October 1st, 2026, arXiv is instituting an updated rate limiting policy across all submitters and categories as a stopgap while we determine what may be the new best practice for authors employing more and more advanced AI tools, and to give us time to improve our moderation tools and procedures accordingly.

Open access repositories across the board are seeing a sharp increase in the number of submissions per author, per month. In September of 2016, arXiv received 9,869 submissions. In September of 2024, arXiv received 20,569 submissions. This September, arXiv received 40,363 submissions, which in turn generated almost 9,000 support tickets for arXiv staff and moderators. In only the past two years, submissions have doubled.

Advanced AI tools are helping drive these increases by making certain aspects of research faster and easier. arXiv policy permits authors to employ AI as a tool in support of their research as long as it is disclosed and the research meets arXiv’s standards of scholarly interest and advances the field of research. However, many of the submissions that arXiv is now receiving do not satisfy these requirements. Our moderators are observing an increase in thin papers of narrow scope, as well as ‘salami’ papers, where a single work is broken up and submitted as a set of smaller papers. There is also a marked increase in dense, AI-written papers. AI tools are making it easy for authors to flood arXiv and other repositories with these low-value papers.

The heart of arXiv’s process for detecting and rejecting low-quality papers is our many volunteer moderators. We are so grateful that they donate their time and expertise every day. However, a relatively small proportion of authors are submitting a large number of low-quality papers and consuming a disproportionate fraction of the moderators’ time. This is unfair to authors who continue to submit quality papers — their papers can be delayed for days or weeks as a result.

arXiv now limits submitters to up to two submissions per calendar month, with a limit of three total active submissions at any given time. This policy update is being put into effect to equitably distribute our volunteer moderators’ time across arXiv authors, and protect the arXiv corpus from a sharp increase in inappropriate submissions.

Rate-limiting is an established arXiv policy, with limiting originally primarily left to moderator discretion. arXiv has always asked that authors follow our codes of conduct and our submission guidelines. Articles submitted to arXiv must be of original, novel, and significant self-contained research that is relevant to arXiv categories. All submissions to arXiv must meet prescribed scholarly standards and be of scholarly interest to the scientific community. This policy update strives to fairly distribute the incredibly valuable work of our volunteer moderators who check that submissions meet these standards, and we hope it will also encourage authors to curate and submit only their best work to arXiv.

Thank you to our scientific community for supporting us in this policy update. We rely on you to help us keep arXiv open, fast, and free, and to help us make sure submissions to arXiv are scientifically rigorous, of interest to the community, and in keeping with current academic standards.

As with all policies, we will continue to monitor the effect of this update on authors, readers, and the arXiv corpus, and modify as needed. Our goal in policy updates is to not only protect arXiv’s corpus, but to improve the arXiv experience for everyone who makes arXiv possible – authors, readers, staff, and all our volunteer moderators.

items.title: Orrore negli Usa, Christa è 'viva ma grave' dopo due iniezioni letali
items.summary: L'avvocato denuncia la 'tortura', bufera sul farmaco ma resta la linea dura
items.content:
Orrore in America, ancora una volta per mano del boia di Stato. In Tennessee Christa Pike, una donna di 50 anni condannata a morte quando era diciottenne per l'assassinio di una coetanea e per 30 anni detenuta nel braccio della morte, é sopravvissuta a due iniezioni letali a base di pentobarbital e il suo avvocato denuncia la tortura.

"E' grave e sta ricvendo cure per salvarle la vita", ha detto il legale Randy Spivey in una conferenza stampa dopo la nuova esecuzione fallita che irrompe nella campagna elettorale per le midterm non tanto per riaprire un serio dibattito sulla pena capitale (negli Usa resta un tabù anche se il consenso cala), ma per dare voce a chi propone il ritorno alla sedia elettrica (la senatrice trumpiana Marsha Blackburn che corre per diventare governatore del Tennessee) e chi invece consiglia di mettere a morte Christa davanti a un plotone di esecuzione. "È la peggiore esecuzione a cui abbiamo assistito, senza precedenti nell'era moderna", ha detto Robin Maher del Death Penalty Information Center andando indietro fino al 1976, quando la Corte Suprema autorizzò gli Stati Usa a tornare all'iniezione letale dopo quattro anni di moratoria nazionale. In Tennessee, nel cui braccio della morte Christa é stata l'unica donna in oltre due secoli, il boia aveva già fallito quest'anno: in maggio non riuscì a trovare le vene di Tony Carruthers, un afroamericano di 57 anni. Dopo circa un'ora e mezza di tentativi l'esecuzione venne annullata. In quel caso il farmaco non fu iniettato, mentre su Pike (che un mese fa aveva chiesto di essere piuttosto impiccata) c'è stata una sorta di accanimento: le due flebo previste dal protocollo sono state somministrate in fretta e furia per tentare di completare l'esecuzione entro la prevista mezzanotte.

Christa tuttavia non é morta. Respirava ancora, rumorosamente, sbatteva le palpebre e, a un certo punto, si é lamentata con il consigliere spirituale: "Il braccio mi brucia, sta per scoppiare. E' normale che vada così?". Attimi drammatici che i testimoni ammessi fuori dalla camera della morte non sono riusciti a ricostruire interamente perché, ad ogni intoppo, venivano chiuse le tendine. Ma questo non ha impedito di suscitare lo sdegno nel Paese e nel resto del mondo. L'alto commissario Onu per i Diritti Umani, Volker Turk, ha chiesto al Tennessee di non tentare ulteriormente: "La sofferenza prolungata, fisica e mentale é abominevole'. Lo stesso governatore del Tennessee, Bill Lee, che lunedì aveva negato la grazia, ha sospeso un'altra esecuzione in programma quest'anno per rivalutare i protocolli falliti. Mentre la candidata Dem al posto di Lee, Jerri Gren, lanciava un appello per la moratoria in nome dei valori "per la vita".

Lo shock non ha però dissuaso i sostenitori della pena di morte: John Yoo, l'ex collaboratore del giudice della Corte suprema Clarence Thomas, ha chiesto sulla Fox che Pike finisca di fronte a un plotone di esecuzione visto il flop del pentobarbital. Il potente anestetico usato per le esecuzioni (ma soprattutto in veterinaria per l'eutanasia di animali) è da anni al centro di polemiche. Il Tennessee lo usa come farmaco unico dopo che il tradizionale cocktail a tre (sodio tiopentale, pentobarbital e bromuro di pancuronio) é diventato difficile da ottenere per le restrizioni imposte all'import da Ue e Regno Unito che boicottano le esecuzioni capitali. E anche l'efficacia e la capacità del barbiturico di garantire una morte senza dolore sono da tempo oggetto di contestazioni. In Tennessee, che ha ripreso a usare il pentobarbital l'anno scorso, la legge consente ai condannati prima del 1999 di optare per la sedia elettrica: dal 2018 è accaduto in cinque casi. Pike era stata condannata nel 1995 per aver ucciso con il suo ragazzo Tadaryl Shipp la 19enne Colleen Slemmer: un delitto brutale dopo il quale Christa, che aveva spaccato il cranio alla vittima con un grosso pezzo di asfalto, ne portò a casa un frammento per ricordo, mentre Taradyl le incise sul petto una stella a cinque punte mentre era ancora viva: un atto che contribuì alla lettura dell'omicidio in chiave satanica. Il ragazzo aveva 17 anni e fu condannato all'ergastolo, mentre a Pike fu comminata la pena di morte senza che venissero prese in considerazione circostanze attenuanti, tra cui le ripetute violenze e gli stupri subite fin da piccolissima: un elemento che in extremis, prima dell'esecuzione, aveva indotto una corte federale a bloccare temporaneamente la mano del boia. Per poi venire contraddetta di li' a poco dalla Corte Suprema.

items.title: La legge elettorale supera il primo scoglio, la maggioranza compatta nel voto segreto
items.summary: Ora faro sull'8 ottobre. Sulle pregiudiziali FnV col centrodestra. Le opposizioni: 'Sarà battaglia'
items.content:
Primo scoglio superato per la maggioranza sulla strada della riforma della legge elettorale . Il centrodestra boccia, a scrutinio segreto, le 5 pregiudiziali di costituzionalità presentate dalle opposizioni in Aula. Dando una notevole prova di compattezza con 229 no. Ai voti del centrodestra si sommano quelli di Futuro Nazionale che spiega di non voler votare "pregiudiziali ridicole" e torna a esprimersi su un voto importante insieme alla maggioranza.

Dall'altro lato Azione critica il testo, ne boccia metodo e tempistica, e vota no con le altre opposizioni. Per il voto segreto a Montecitorio - anche dopo i messaggi della premier negli ultimi giorni - si registra il pienone delle grandi occasioni: nel centrodestra, tabulati alla mano, risultano soli 7 deputati assenti su 233 e 3 in missione, tra cui la premier e il ministro Gilberto Pichetto Fratin. E anche dalle parti delle opposizioni già dalla prima mattina i banchi sono pieni e si fanno vedere tutti i leader. Ora gli occhi sono puntati sull'8 ottobre, con il voto finale, segreto, che dovrà dare il via libera alla riforma. Un voto che, non nasconde il responsabile organizzazione di FdI, Giovanni Donzelli, "ha un valore politico enorme". Ma al quale il centrodestra, dopo la prova di oggi, si avvicina con qualche pensiero in meno.

"A livello parlamentare è andata", pronostica in barba alla scaramanzia, un esponente leghista commentando l'esito di oggi, poi "bisognerà vedere la Consulta". Da qui ad allora c'è comunque la prossima decisiva settimana: lunedì il governo in mattinata metterà tre fiducie sui primi tre articoli del provvedimento che sono stati modificati al Senato. I primi due (sui quali sono stati presentati in Aula una sessantina di emendamenti) riguardano preferenze e firme. Il terzo, che verrà votato mercoledì sempre con fiducia, riguarda una revisione territoriale dei collegi di Merano, Bolzano e Bressanone. Sul punto non ci sono emendamenti ma è comunque possibile chiedere il voto segreto sull'articolo. E dunque, per evitare di mostrare il fianco a eventuali malpancisti della maggioranza, approfittando di questa norma più 'piccola', anche qui verrà messa la fiducia. Si voterà invece senza fiducia ma a scrutinio palese (perché su questa materia non direttamente legata alla trasformazione dei voti in seggi chiedere il segreto non possibile) sulla modifica all'articolo 8 riguardante l'estensione del voto dei fuorisede ai caregiver, non ci sono comunque emendamenti ed è stato votato a Palazzo Madama all'unanimità. A questo punto, dopo l'esame degli ordini del giorno nel pomeriggio del 7 ottobre, il giorno successivo alle 12.30 si terrà il voto finale sul testo. E se la maggioranza ha tirato, per ora, un sospiro di sollievo, l'opposizione si prepara a proseguire la sua battaglia. Puntando anche a sfruttare la riforma del sistema di voto per ricreare lo spirito referendario del marzo scorso.

"Se questo vostro scempio sarò approvato - dice il Dem Gianni Cuperlo - dal giorno successivo la battaglia si trasferirà fuori da queste Aule nel Paese e nelle piazze con un'Italia che non si piega, come avvenuto sul Referendum". Intanto, in Aula, le accuse si moltiplicano. "Questa è una maggioranza disperata che cerca di imbullonarsi al potere", attacca M5s. "E' incostituzionale, l'ennesima forzatura", sottolinea Nicola Fratoianni di Avs. Mentre Roberto Giachetti va all'attacco del fatto che, anche con questa legge "una parte determinante degli eletti è predeterminata dai partiti". "Tra le norme più incostituzionali ed antidemocratiche di questa legge elettorale c'è quella dell'innalzamento delle sottoscrizioni necessarie per presentarsi alle elezioni" dice Riccardo Magi tornando a fare un appello per le firme digitali per il quale prosegue il suo sciopero della fame.

items.title: Netanyahu says Flydubai attacker had 'Islamist radical indoctrination'
items.summary: Israel's prime minister says the pilot who tried to take over the Flydubai plane clearly intended to "down the plane".
items.content:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu says investigations suggest the man who stabbed his fellow pilot and tried to take over a flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv had undergone "Islamist radical indoctrination".

The Flydubai plane plunged more than 17,000ft (5,200m) two hours into its journey on Wednesday, before passengers and crew overpowered the attacker and retook control to land safely.

Netanyahu told Fox News that it was looking "very likely" that the attacker, who he said was an Omani national, "was going to down the plane".

Meanwhile, the United Arab Emirates (UAE) state news agency reports investigations have begun there to determine "whether the incident was linked to any terrorist activity or purpose".

The Interior Ministry of Saudi Arabia - where the plane made an emergency landing - said that both the pilot and co-pilot had been sent back to the UAE on Thursday morning after medical teams had cleared them.

UAE officials earlier claimed jurisdiction over the incident because the aircraft on which the attack took place is registered there and flies under its flag.

Netanyahu told Fox that once the attacker had been subdued and tied up by passengers and crew, he was "calling out to the aircrew 'kill me, kill me', so it's clear he was suicidal - that's not a question".

"And with all the passengers in there, and if you couple that with what I just told you about the Islamist tendencies, that radicalisation that were found in his background, I think... that'll give us a pretty good clue."

However, he stressed that he did not want to draw any firm conclusions as to motive yet.

Both US President Donald Trump and UAE officials have indicated to the media that Iran may be responsible for the incident, without definitively blaming Tehran.

Trump told reporters on Thursday that Iran would be "hit very hard" if it was deemed to have been involved in the attack.

Pilots from countries without diplomatic relations with Israel were usually not allowed to fly there, Netanyahu said when asked about how the suspected Omani pilot came to be on the plane.

He added: "Obviously there was a loophole here and we're taking care of that among other things... with the full co-operation, I have to say, of the Emirati government, so we're both interested in making sure this doesn't happen again."

Oman has not formally established official ties with Israel , unlike the UAE.

The prime minister was also asked earlier on the same network whether there was an indication if Iran was involved, he replied: "It's too early to say".

Flydubai passenger describes hugging his children as plane nosedived during attack

Who is the 'hero' Indian pilot who was stabbed on Israel-bound flight?

Both Netanyahu and Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi said the stabbed pilot, Indian national Capt Smit Machchhar was a "hero".

India's ambassador to the UAE Deepak Mittal visited Captain Machhar in hospital on Thursday, the Indian Mission confirmed on social media, stating he was "in good health and recovering well".

Preliminary findings from a separate Israeli investigation into the incident, suggest that the alleged attacker intended to crash the plane, an Israeli security source told BBC Arabic.

The source said the investigation - led by Israel's intelligence agency Mossad - interviewed passengers after they arrived in Tel Aviv to establish what had happened on the plane.

Flydubai's flight FZ1073, with more than 170 people on board, took off from Dubai International Airport in the UAE at 03:05 GMT (07:05 local time), en route to Ben Gurion Airport.

Two hours later, the 17,000ft drop in altitude was reported on the plane tracking website Flightradar24 and minutes later the plane signalled an emergency code.

At about 05:40, the plane - which had briefly entered Jordanian airspace - looped back into Saudi Arabia, where it later started its manual descent, landing safely at Tabuk Airport in the north west of Saudi.

Flydubai has since suspended flights between Dubai and Tel Aviv as it carried out its own investigation into the incident.

Israel's Transportation Ministry said the suspension aligns with Netanyahu's directive.

Israeli airlines including El Al, Israir and Arkia said plans were in place to operate rescue flights from Dubai starting on Friday to bring back stranded passengers.

The Transportation Ministry also said it sent an urgent request to Etihad Airlines to increase the number of flights between Abu Dhabi and Tel Aviv.
